environment.description: Same Django REST API deployed on ECS Fargate behind an ALB. The HMAC secret used for HS256 verification is sourced from AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation configured at a 60-second interval via a Lambda rotator (rotation uses AWSCURRENT/AWSPENDING staging labels with immediate version deprecation). The Secrets Manager resource policy restricts GetSecretValue to the ECS task execution role only. Additionally, the application container runs with a read-only root filesystem and the JWT_HMAC_SECRET environment variable is injected at task start from the AWSCURRENT version. When the secret rotates (every 60s), the ECS service performs a rolling deployment triggered by a CloudWatch Events rule on the SecretsManager RotationSucceeded event, meaning the in-memory HMAC secret in any running container is never more than ~65 seconds stale relative to AWSCURRENT. An attacker who obtains the public RSA key (which is intentionally public) and crafts an HS256 token using the public key as the HMAC secret will find that the application's JWT_HMAC_SECRET environment variable contains a completely different value (the Secrets Manager-managed random secret), so HMAC verification against the RSA public key material will fail with an InvalidSignatureError.

config.hmac_secret_injection: ECS task definition environment from AWSCURRENT
config.ecs_task_role_policy: secretsmanager:GetSecretValue restricted to task role ARN
